yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every technical point kept with code, links and numbers intact: "the FOLD waits its turn in an exit queue", "From Unix timestamp **`1787148000`** on, anyone could call the `tge()` function", the four setup steps, the operator-only bonding. Nothing added.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Mostly exact: "keeps the economic side of the network ticking over", "It can also cop penalties for provable", "have a squiz at", "If you need a hand". "for not pulling its weight on assigned responsibilities" puts the failure on the bonded FOLD rather than the operator, a slight strain.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian technical-doc voice: "If you're after supply and allocation data", "Mind you, general FOLD transferability and Network Alpha are two separate milestones". "Nah, nah." as an FAQ answer is a bit stagey.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light-to-moderate touch fitting level 2: "keen", "ticking over", "cop penalties", "pulling its weight", "have a squiz", "Nah, nah.", "need a hand", "jump into".
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays a clear, neutral FAQ; the softeners don't undercut it: "The Interfold's bonding model is operator-only, and that's on purpose."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth, with good joins: "Applications ask for Encrypted" and "Delegated capital would let operators run part-owned ciphernodes, which would water down".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied, nothing leaned on: "ticking over", "hang together", "cop", "pulling its weight", "pick up FOLD incentives", "Mind you", "have a squiz", "water down".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the FOLD token FAQ, structure, headings, code and links intact.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All technical facts survive, but it adds claims and readings: "First in, best dressed." (implies a race with a prize to call `tge()`), "And someone was quick off the mark", "Everyone's on the hook, so nobody is.", "which is a neat trick when you think about it", "FOLD is the money side of it". The 23-second gap is correct arithmetic but presented as an achievement.
yarn-troppo.sense: Several fit ("doing the yakka", "it can get a guernsey on E3 committees", "the whole box and dice", "have a squiz"). But "First in, best dressed." takes the wrong sense: anyone could call the function, with no advantage for being first.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Genuinely Australian idiom ("get a guernsey", "yakka", "sing out", "box and dice"), but many lines are bolted-on tags: "Do the work, get a cut.", "No ticket, no ride.", "Muck up, and it's your bond that pays."
yarn-troppo.register: Far heavier than level 2 for a technical FAQ: "Here's the lowdown on what FOLD actually does", "Now the good bit.", "nobody's standing at the door with a clipboard", "Stuck?".
yarn-troppo.tone: A neutral, precise FAQ turned chatty and salesy: "Now the good bit.", "which is a neat trick when you think about it", "Do the work, get a cut."
yarn-troppo.flow: Readable, but the tag lines interrupt the explanation: "balance. No ticket, no ride. See", "So, the Interfold. It's a distributed network".
yarn-troppo.variety: Many different idioms, but the punchy tag-sentence device recurs and "sing out" appears twice ("Applications sing out", "and sing out").
yarn-troppo.essence: Structure and facts are there, but a precise reference page now reads like a pitch: "Think of it as putting your money where your mouth is."

engine.meaning: The original verbatim apart from "Nah, nah." replacing "No.", so every point is kept.
engine.sense: The one term, "Nah, nah.", carries the original 'No.'.
engine.authenticity: "Nah, nah." is bolted onto otherwise untouched formal US prose: "Nah, nah. The bonding model of the Interfold is deliberately operator-only.", with "misbehavior" and "fulfill" left in.
engine.register: Left almost entirely untranslated: "This FAQ explains what FOLD does in the Interfold network. It is for token holders and for people".
engine.tone: The original's neutral tone, except the jarring "Nah, nah."
engine.flow: Reads as the original, with one jolt: "Nah, nah. The bonding model of the Interfold is deliberately operator-only."
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, being the original.

yarn-deadset.register: Light, slightly under level 2: "cop", "Nah, nah.", "water down", "need a hand", "info"; much of the text stays close to the original.
yarn-deadset.tone: Neutral and clear throughout: "The operator sets the bond owner."
yarn-deadset.flow: Clean, with a couple of stiff phrasings: "FOLD backs the economic running of the network.", "These mechanisms line up operational".

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept, nothing added: "the FOLD sits in an exit queue", "Ciphernode operators get a cut of the fees from completed E3s", "capital on the line for the operator who runs it".
unharnessed.sense: All fit: "anyone keen to run a ciphernode", "cop penalties", "a cut of the fees", "To be in the running for committee selection", "water down", "jump into".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, understated Australian English: "It's for token holders and for anyone", "No. The Interfold's bonding model is operator-only, and that's on purpose."
unharnessed.register: Light, around level 2 or a touch under: "keen", "cop", "a cut", "in the running", "on the line", "water down", "need a hand", "jump into".

summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful, natural and at the right weight; the best balance of the set.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Rich in real idiom, but far too heavy for level-2 docs, salesy in tone, and one idiom implies a race that didn't exist.
